title: Nicaea II’s fathers distinguish adoration from mere veneration—and call hypocrites those who venerate but refuse to adore
source_text: VI. Porro Patres istius Synodi adorationem illam, quam imaginibus deferendam putant, a veneratione distinguunt, tanquam quae plus aliquid importet quam simplex veneratio. Etenim damnant illos qui se quidem imagines venerari confitentur, sed tamen illas adorare recusant. Ut videre est Actione quarta, ubi post Lecta quaedam verba Anastasii Episcopi Theopolitani, sic loquitur Tharasius Patriarcha, Omnes igitur qui sacras imagines se venerari confitentur, adorationem autem recusant a sancto Patre tanquam hypocritae redarguuntur. Nam cum vere adorationem, quod est honoris symbolum recusant, contrarium facere cognoscuntur, nimirum sanctis convitia dicere. Tomi jam citati pag. 335.
pass_a_gloss: Further, the Fathers of that Synod distinguish that adoration which they think is to be paid to images from veneration, as importing something more than simple veneration. For they condemn those who indeed confess that they venerate images, but yet refuse to adore them. As may be seen in the fourth Action, where after certain words of Anastasius Bishop of Theopolis had been read, Tarasius the Patriarch speaks thus: All therefore who confess that they venerate sacred images, but refuse adoration, are refuted by the holy Father as hypocrites. For when they refuse true adoration, which is a symbol of honor, they are known to do the contrary, namely to speak insults to the saints. Tom. already cited, p. 335.
pass_b_english: The Synod’s adoration is more than bare veneration.
Those who say they venerate images but will not adore them are branded hypocrites who insult the saints.

choices.why: Adoration is treated as the honor-sign veneration alone does not carry.
